questions.question:
Let $p$ and $p + 2$ be prime numbers and let

$\Delta = \left( \begin{matrix}p! & \left(p + 1\right)! & \left(p + 2\right)! \\ \left(p + 1\right)! & \left(p + 2\right)! & \left(p + 3\right)! \\ \left(p + 2\right)! & \left(p + 3\right)! & \left(p + 4\right)!\end{matrix} \right)$

Then the sum of the maximum values of $\alpha$ and $\beta$, such that ${p}^{\alpha }$ and ${\left(p + 2\right)}^{\beta }$ divide $\Delta$, is _______.
questions.explanation:
Given,

$\Delta = \left( \begin{matrix}P! & \left(P + 1\right)! & \left(P + 2\right)! \\ \left(P + 1\right)! & \left(P + 2\right)! & \left(P + 3\right)! \\ \left(P + 2\right)! & \left(P + 3\right)! & \left(P + 4\right)!\end{matrix} \right)$

Now using the factorial concept and taking common terms we get,

$\implies \Delta = P!\left(P + 1\right)!\left(P + 2\right)!\left( \begin{matrix}1 & 1 & 1 \\ P + 1 & P + 2 & P + 3 \\ \left(P + 2\right)\left(P + 1\right) & \left(P + 3\right)\left(P + 2\right) & \left(P + 4\right)\left(P + 3\right)\end{matrix} \right)$

Now on solving determinant we get, $\left( \begin{matrix}1 & 1 & 1 \\ P + 1 & P + 2 & P + 3 \\ \left(P + 2\right)\left(P + 1\right) & \left(P + 3\right)\left(P + 2\right) & \left(P + 4\right)\left(P + 3\right)\end{matrix} \right)$

Using operation ${C}_{1} \to {C}_{1} - {C}_{2} & {C}_{2} \to {C}_{2} - {C}_{3} \left( \begin{matrix}0 & 0 & 1 \\ - 1 & - 1 & P + 3 \\ - 2P - 4 & - 2P - 6 & \left(P + 4\right)\left(P + 3\right)\end{matrix} \right) = 2P + 6 - \left(2P + 4\right) = 2$

Now putting the value of determinant we get,

$\implies \Delta = 2P!\left(P + 1\right)!\left(P + 2\right)! \implies \Delta = 2{P}^{3}\left(P - 1\right)!\left(P + 1\right)\left(P - 1\right)!\left(P + 2\right)\left(P + 1\right)\left(P - 1\right)!$

Which is divisible by ${P}^{\alpha }$ and ${\left(P + 2\right)}^{\beta }$

So, $\alpha = 3,\beta = 1$

The system of equations ${a}_{1}x + {b}_{1}y + {c}_{1}z = 0,{a}_{2}x + {b}_{2}y + {c}_{2}z = 0$ and ${a}_{3}x + {b}_{3}y + {c}_{3}z = 0$ has a non-trivial solution, if

$\left( \begin{matrix}{a}_{1} & {b}_{1} & {c}_{1} \\ {a}_{2} & {b}_{2} & {c}_{2} \\ {a}_{3} & {b}_{3} & {c}_{3}\end{matrix} \right) = 0.$

Hence, for the given lines $2x + 3y - z = 0,x + ky - 2z = 0$ and $2x - y + z = 0,$ we have

$\left( \begin{matrix}2 & 3 & - 1 \\ 1 & k & - 2 \\ 2 & - 1 & 1\end{matrix} \right) = 0 \implies 2\left(k - 2\right) - 3\left(1 + 4\right) - 1\left( - 1 - 2k\right) = 0 \implies 2k - 4 - 15 + 1 + 2k = 0 \implies k = \frac{9}{2}$

Thus, the lines are

$2x + 3y - z = 0...\left(1\right) x + \frac{9}{2}y - 2z = 0...\left(2\right) 2x - y + z = 0...\left(3\right) \left(1\right) - \left(3\right) \implies 4y - 2z = 0 2y = z...\left(4\right) \frac{y}{z} = \frac{1}{2}...\left(5\right)$

put $z$ from eq $\left(4\right)$ into $\left(1\right) 2x + 3y - 2y = 0 2x + y = 0 \frac{x}{y} = - \frac{1}{2}...\left(6\right)$

From eq $\left(4\right)$ and $\left(6\right) \frac{z}{x} = - 4$

Hence, $\frac{x}{y} + \frac{y}{z} + \frac{z}{x} + k = - \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{2} - 4 + \frac{9}{2} = \frac{1}{2}.$

$2a + b = 1\;$

The system of equations are
